dedupe_keys.name: nigeria interactive web gis of open data for fresh produce supply chains

description: This case study builds an interactive web map that gathers open data on Nigeria's agriculture to support decisions that reduce loss in fresh produce supply chains. The authors, researchers at the Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology (Empa) and Constructor University, collected tabular, vector and raster open datasets, processed them in open-source GIS and web computing platforms, and published the layers on a consolidated map built on Google Earth Engine; the method is published as an open-access journal article so that other countries can reproduce it. Layers include crop production, market prices, weather, the road network, market locations, mobile coverage, water access and scarcity, and food insecurity. Coverage is national. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence, and the map is public online; source datasets keep their own terms. Caveats: layers come from sources with different dates and resolutions, and the map may not be maintained. The study showed that scattered open data can be combined into one tool for supply chain stakeholders. Simulation uses: a ready collection of inputs, such as markets, roads and production, for food supply chain and cold chain models in Nigeria. Related records: the Nigeria health facility registry extract (data-nigeria-health-facility-registry-extract) is another national open infrastructure layer.
